full_judgment: 8. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. It appears, in the first place, that the matter contains a disputed question of facts with regard to the number of population which this Court cannot, in its writ jurisdiction, go into and decide without taking evidence about the number of population in each of the said Union Parishads or any Mouzas. It also appears from Rule 2(4) that an appeal has to be made within seven days before the Deputy Commissioner or Divisional Commissioner, as the case may be; but in the present case no such appeal has been made within the said period of seven days and the appeal that has been filed vide Annexure-F to the supplementary affidavit dated 19.11.91 is about 5 months after the Gazette Notification dated 20.6.91. This Gazette Notification has been made by the Deputy Commissioner under sub-rule 6 of Rule 2 on the orders of the Government after going through all the formalities under the provisions of section 114 of the Evidence Act by the officials of the Government which is presumed to be done in accordance with the rules and procedure unless it has been proved otherwise. The illustration (c) of section 114 of the Evidence Act provides that all acts are presumed to have been rightly and regularly done. This presumption applies to judicial as well as to official acts. Presumption under section 88 is another presumption in favour of regularity of acts. Thus where judicial or official act is shown to have been done, it is presumed to have been done rightly and regularly complying with the necessary requirements.
